title: Online Threshold Learner for Microbatch Admission and KV-slot Reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS we see repeated oscillations between accepted micro-batch sizes and sudden KV cache evictions that spike p95 latency. Existing heuristics in the admission controller use static watermarks and simple exponentially-smoothed headroom metrics which fail to adapt quickly to workload shifts (burstiness and varying token length distributions).

Proposal: Implement a lightweight online threshold learner that observes short-term GPU memory slope (delta bytes per second), admission acceptance rate, and micro-batch completion latency to continuously adjust micro-batching admission thresholds and KV-slot reclaim aggressiveness. The learner is a low-cost logistic-regression-style model (online SGD with L2) that outputs a per-GPU threshold score (0..1) used to gate micro-batch acceptance probabilistically. A secondary probabilistic drop mechanism reclaims low-priority KV slots when the score crosses a reclaim threshold. The design is intentionally conservative: the learned thresholds are combined with safety floors/ceilings and an inertia term to avoid oscillation.

Goals: reduce p95 token latency regressions during sustained high QPS by 20%, reduce tail KV-eviction events by 30%, and avoid throughput loss greater than 5% compared to current admission policy during steady-state workloads.
implementation_notes: Place learner in admission controller module next to existing headroom estimator
Expose metrics: learner_score, learner_loss, probabilistic_accept_count, kv_reclaim_actions
acceptance_criteria: Learner can be toggled per-cluster via feature flag
No user-facing errors introduced; admission controller falls back to static thresholds if learner process fails
Automated canary tests show p95 latency improvement >= 10% on at least 3 synthetic burst patterns and no throughput loss > 5%
test_plan: Unit tests for online update step, deterministic simulation harness for replaying production traces
Canary on a small Dedicated pool with synthetic QPS profiles (sine bursts, Poisson bursts, long-tail token lengths)
A/B experiment with 1% of traffic for 48h capturing p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction counts, and per-token cost
rollout_plan: Dev-only smoke test -> staging 6h soak -> canary 1% traffic 48h -> ramp to 10% 24h -> full rollout with rollback windows
Observe automated alerts for eviction_rate spike or sudden drop in throughput
notes: This approach intentionally keeps the ML model tiny to avoid lifecycle burden — parameters and checkpoints are ephemeral and not persisted long-term
If learner shows promise, follow-up will evaluate a per-model variant learner (different behavior for long-context LLMs)
Coordination needed with the KV team for safe reclaim semantics — ensure low-priority slots map to test cohorts first
comments: 2025-11-03: Spike complete — initial simulation shows learner reduces eviction bursts in the 'sine-burst' profile by 28% (simulation-only). - Jonas

2025-11-05: Design review with PM and KV owner. Agree to add a safety floor and inertia term; KV reclaim will only target 'ephemeral' slots flagged by the cache index. Action: add doc section for reclaim target classification. - Aisha

2025-11-09: Prototype integrated with admission controller. Observed a rare oscillation when combined with autoscaler bursts; mitigated by adding a 3s minimum hold time on threshold changes. Need longer canary. - Jonas
2025-11-14: Load test (staging) 24h summary attached: p95 latency down 12%, kv_eviction_rate down 21%, throughput -1.6%. Going to canary 1% tomorrow. - Aisha
